'''Franklin Gerardus "Frank" Grosveld,''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (born 18 August 1948, died 25 June 2026)<ref>‘GROSVELD, Prof. Franklin Gerardus, (Frank)’, Who's Who 2013, A & C Black, an imprint of Bloomsbury Publishing plc, 2013; online edn, Oxford University Press, Dec 2012; online edn, Nov 2012 [http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U18332 accessed 31 Oct 2013]</ref> was a Dutch molecular biologist whose research interests are in the regulation of transcription during development with a particular emphasis on mammalian [[erythroid]] differentiation. He is a professor and former Head of the Department of Cell Biology at the [[Erasmus MC]], Rotterdam.

==Biography==
He obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree from [[McGill University]], Montreal and after completing two postdoctoral periods with [[Charles Weissmann]] (Zurich) and [[Richard Flavell]] (Amsterdam and London) he started his own research group at the [[National Institute for Medical Research]], Mill Hill.

Grosveld has been conducting research on the regulation of [[gene expression]] over thirty years. In his post-doctoral research he constructed the first reliable method for [[cloning]] human DNA [[cosmid]]s - at the time an extremely difficult but rewarding accomplishment that has since been adopted by many other laboratories. By using the [[globin]] gene cluster he made the ground-breaking discovery of a [[locus control region]] located upstream of the gene itself and governing overall control of [[globin]] [[gene expression]]. After this first report, [[locus control region]]s have now been identified for many genes and have permitted for example the [[ectopic expression]] of genes in [[transgenic mice]]. In further studies he identified [[chromatin]] loops and the hubs that hold the loops together. His more recent excursions into [[erythroid]] differentiation have made the key identification of the [[transcription factor]] [[GATA1]], a major and unique advance into understanding [[erythroid]] cell development. Along with major research advances he has also developed new technologies, such as 4C technology (a modification of the 3C technology invented previously by others) that makes possible examination of [[chromatin]] conformation on a chip and constructed a number of spin off companies. He has mentored a large number of PhDs and postdocs, many of whom have gone on to academic positions all over the world and are now eminent scientists leading groups of their own.<ref name="knaw.nl">{{Cite web |url=http://www.knaw.nl/professorship/2008.html |title=KNAW > Academy Professorships Programme > 2007 |access-date=2009-08-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101103130919/http://knaw.nl/professorship/2008.html |archive-date=2010-11-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Grosveld's research on the control of [[globin]] [[gene expression]] has been selected as one of the top ten achievements of [[Medical Research Council (UK)]] (MRC) in the 20th century by Higher Education and Research Opportunities in the UK.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://admin.hero.ac.uk/sites/hero/uk/research/research_outcomes/medical_science_209.cfm |title=Medical science |access-date=2009-08-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090916070220/http://admin.hero.ac.uk/sites/hero/uk/research/research_outcomes/medical_science_209.cfm |archive-date=2009-09-16 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was awarded the [[Louis-Jeantet Prize for Medicine]] (1991) and the [[Spinozapremie]] (Spinoza Prize) (1995).<ref>{{cite web |author= |url=http://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/spinoza+prize/spinoza+laureates/overview+by+year/1995 |title=NWO Spinoza Prize 1995 |publisher=Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research |date=3 September 2014 |accessdate=30 January 2016 |archive-date=29 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150629053424/http://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/spinoza+prize/spinoza+laureates/overview+by+year/1995 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was selected as academy professor of [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2008.<ref name="knaw.nl"/>

He was a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) and [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences|Member of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] since 1994.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.biomedcentral.com/independent/profiles/715101 |title=BioMed Central {{!}} editor profiles |website=www.biomedcentral.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081121202202/http://biomedcentral.com/independent/profiles/715101 |archive-date=2008-11-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/nl/leden/leden/4190 |title=Frank Grosveld |language=Dutch |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |accessdate=14 July 2015}}</ref>
